answer: Used Cambridge Dictionary's Grammar section and opened the dedicated page 'Comparison: adjectives (bigger, biggest, more interesting)' (https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/comparison-adjectives-bigger-biggest-more-interesting). Formation rules: one-syllable adjectives add -er/-est (tall-taller-tallest); spelling rules apply (big-bigger, nice-nicer, happy-happier); longer adjectives use more/most (more interesting, most expensive); irregular forms exist (good-better-best, bad-worse-worst, far-farther/further). Usage rules: comparatives are followed by 'than' (Josh is taller than his sister); much/a lot/far strengthen comparatives; superlatives take 'the' and can be followed by prepositional phrases (the tallest of/in). Extracted 46 example sentences from the page, e.g. 'Josh is taller than his sister.', 'I'm more interested in music than sport.', 'The most frightening film I've ever seen was Alfred Hitchcock's Psycho.'
